whys.why: Since 1 M = 1000 mM, multiplying by 1000 mM/M cancels M and moves the decimal point three places to the right.

whys.title: Exercise \(\PageIndex{2}\)
whys.question: What is the molarity after 15.0 mL of 6.00 M HCl is diluted to 250.0 mL?
whys.why: The moles of HCl do not change on dilution, so M<sub>2</sub> = M<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub>/V<sub>2</sub>; the mL units cancel because both volumes are in mL.

whys.title: Exercise \(\PageIndex{3}\)
whys.question: What volume of 2.00 M KCl stock is needed to prepare 100.0 mL of 0.0500 M KCl?
whys.why: All the moles in the final solution come from the stock, so V<sub>1</sub> = M<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub>/M<sub>1</sub>; the stock is 40 times as concentrated, so you need one-fortieth of 100.0 mL.

whys.title: Exercise \(\PageIndex{1}\)
whys.question: Write K for 2 SO 2 (g) + O 2 (g) ⇄ 2 SO 3 (g).
whys.why: Products go on top and reactants on the bottom, each raised to its coefficient: 2 for SO<sub>3</sub> and SO<sub>2</sub>, 1 (not written) for O<sub>2</sub>; all three are gases, so none is left out.

whys.title: Exercise \(\PageIndex{1}\)
whys.question: A piece of charcoal from an ancient fire pit has 50.0% of the carbon-14 of living wood. How old is it?
whys.why: One half-life leaves 50% of the original carbon-14, and the half-life of carbon-14 is 5730 years.

bank.question: What mass of Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (142.04 g/mol) is needed to prepare 100.0 mL of 0.450 M Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>?
bank.new_reason: This uses mL as liters. Convert 100.0 mL to 0.1000 L before multiplying by the molarity.

bank.question: How many nitrogen atoms are in 0.0750 mol of ammonium nitrate, NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub>?
bank.new_reason: This stops at moles of N. Multiply the moles of N by Avogadro's number, 6.0221 × 10<sup>23</sup>, to count atoms.

bank.question: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 4.75 g of MgCl<sub>2</sub> (95.21 g/mol) in enough water to make 150.0 mL of solution?
bank.new_reason: This divides by mL; convert to L. Molarity is moles per liter, so use 0.1500 L.

bank.question: Calcium dihydrogen phosphate, Ca(H<sub>2</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub> (234.04 g/mol), is a phosphorus fertilizer. What is its mass percent of phosphorus? (P 30.97)
bank.new_reason: This is the percent of calcium. Put the mass of phosphorus, 2 × 30.97, over the molar mass.

bank.question: A 0.1700 g sample of oxalic acid, H<sub>2</sub>C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> (90.034 g/mol), needs 25.85 mL of NaOH to reach the endpoint. What is the molarity of the NaOH? H<sub>2</sub>C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>(aq) + 2 NaOH(aq) → Na<sub>2</sub>C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>(aq) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l)
bank.new_reason: This uses grams as moles. Convert 0.1700 g to moles with 90.034 g/mol, then use the 2 : 1 ratio.

bank.question: A Valley dairy digester burns captured methane, CH<sub>4</sub>(g) + 2 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l), ΔH = −890.3 kJ. What mass of methane must burn to release 3.60 × 10<sup>4</sup> kJ? (CH<sub>4</sub> 16.043 g/mol)
bank.worked: 3.60 × 104 kJ × (1 mol CH4 / 890.3 kJ) × (16.043 g / 1 mol) = 649 g CH4.
bank.new_reason: This stops at moles of methane. Multiply by 16.043 g/mol to convert moles to grams.

bank.question: What volume of N<sub>2</sub> at STP is needed to make 0.875 mol of NH<sub>3</sub>? N<sub>2</sub>(g) + 3 H<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2 NH<sub>3</sub>(g)
bank.worked: 0.875 mol NH3 × (1 mol N2 / 2 mol NH3) × (22.4 L / 1 mol) = 9.80 L N2.
bank.new_reason: This stops at moles. Multiply the moles of N<sub>2</sub> by 22.4 L/mol to get liters at STP.

bank.question: Sodium phosphate, Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>, dissolves into Na<sup>+</sup> and PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup> ions. How many moles of ions in total come from 0.0200 mol of Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>?
bank.worked: 0.0200 mol × 4 mol ions / 1 mol = 0.0800 mol ions.
bank.new_reason: This counts only the sodium ions. Each Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> gives 3 Na<sup>+</sup> and 1 PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup>, so multiply by 4 ions per formula unit.

bank.question: Which statement describes what happens inside the nucleus during positron emission?
choices: A proton changes into a neutron, so Z decreases by 1 and A stays the same.
A neutron changes into a proton, so Z increases by 1 and A stays the same.
The nucleus captures an inner electron, so A decreases by 1.
The nucleus releases only energy, so A and Z stay the same.
bank.worked: Positron emission: proton → neutron + positron; Z − 1, A unchanged.
bank.new_reason: That is gamma emission. In positron emission a proton becomes a neutron, so Z drops by 1 and A stays the same.

bank.question: How many valence electrons are in the carbonate ion, CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup>?
bank.new_reason: This counts one O atom: 4 + 6 + 2. Multiply by the subscript: three O atoms give 3 × 6.

bank.question: What is the limiting reactant in a reaction?
choices: The reactant that is used up first, which sets the most product that can form
The reactant present in the smallest mass
The reactant with the smallest coefficient in the balanced equation
The reactant that is left over when the reaction stops
bank.worked: The limiting reactant is used up first and sets the maximum amount of product; the other reactant is in excess and some is left over.
bank.new_reason: That is the excess reactant. The limiting reactant runs out first, so it decides how much product can form.

bank.question: Carbon tetrachloride, CCl<sub>4</sub>, has polar C–Cl bonds and a symmetric tetrahedral shape. What is its strongest intermolecular force?
bank.new_reason: CCl<sub>4</sub> has no hydrogen at all, so it cannot hydrogen bond. Its bond dipoles cancel in the symmetric shape, so it is nonpolar.

bank.question: Milk of magnesia neutralizes stomach acid: Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub>(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → MgCl<sub>2</sub>(aq) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l). What mass of HCl can 0.350 g of Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub> neutralize? (Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub> 58.32 g/mol; HCl 36.46 g/mol)
bank.worked: 0.350 g × (1 mol / 58.32 g) × (2 mol HCl / 1 mol) × (36.46 g / 1 mol) = 0.438 g HCl. (Context only; follow the label.)
bank.new_reason: This uses the coefficient twice. Apply the 2 mol HCl / 1 mol Mg(OH)<sub>2</sub> ratio only once in the chain.

bank.question: For molecules of similar size, which list orders the forces from weakest to strongest?
bank.worked: Dispersion < dipole–dipole < hydrogen bond < ion–dipole (for similar sizes).
bank.new_reason: This list is reversed. Weakest to strongest starts with dispersion and ends with ion–dipole.

bank.question: How many milliliters of 0.425 M KCl stock are needed to make 200.0 mL of 12.5 mM KCl?
bank.new_reason: This divides by V<sub>2</sub>. Solve M<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> = M<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub> for V<sub>1</sub>: multiply M<sub>2</sub> by V<sub>2</sub>, then divide by M<sub>1</sub>.

bank.question: Rank K, Mg and Cl in order of increasing atomic radius.
bank.worked: Smallest at the upper right, largest at the lower left: Cl < Mg < K.
bank.new_reason: This is decreasing radius. Radius grows toward the lower left of the table, so list from the upper-right element (smallest) to the lower-left one (largest).

bank.question: Methane burns: CH<sub>4</sub>(g) + 2 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(g). A 2.85 L sample of CH<sub>4</sub>, measured at STP, burns completely. What volume of O<sub>2</sub>, measured at 1.05 atm and 21.5 °C, is used?
bank.new_reason: This skips the mole ratio. Multiply moles of CH<sub>4</sub> by 2 mol O<sub>2</sub> / 1 mol CH<sub>4</sub> before using PV = nRT.

bank.question: What is the name of HIO<sub>4</sub>?
bank.worked: IO4− = periodate; -ate → -ic, prefix kept: periodic acid (per-iodic, nothing to do with the periodic table).
bank.new_reason: Oxyacids never take hydro-; hydro- is only for acids with no oxygen. Name it from the anion: periodate (-ate) becomes periodic acid (-ic).

bank.question: Methane burns: CH<sub>4</sub>(g) + 2 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(g). A 2.85 L sample of CH<sub>4</sub>, measured at STP, burns completely. What volume of O<sub>2</sub>, measured at 1.05 atm and 21.5 °C, is used?
bank.new_reason: This uses the Celsius temperature. Gas laws need kelvins: add 273.15 to 21.5 °C before using PV = nRT.

bank.question: A respiratory therapy chart lists inhaled “NO” as a gas used for some newborns. What does NO stand for?
choices: A compound made of nitrogen and oxygen
bank.worked: A symbol has one capital letter, so NO is two symbols, N and O: the compound nitric oxide. Compare No (nobelium) and CO (carbon monoxide) with Co (cobalt).
bank.new_reason: Neon's symbol is Ne. A symbol has only one capital letter, so a capital N followed by a capital O means two symbols: N and O.

bank.question: How many hydrogen atoms are in 5.00 g of ethanol, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (46.069 g/mol)?
bank.worked: 5.00 g × (1 mol / 46.069 g) × (6 mol H / 1 mol) × 6.0221 × 1023 = 3.92 × 1023 H atoms.
bank.new_reason: This stops at moles of H. Multiply the moles of H by Avogadro's number, 6.0221 × 10<sup>23</sup>, to count atoms.

bank.question: How many moles of KCl are in 42.5 mL of 0.0875 M KCl?
bank.new_reason: This uses mL in place of L. Convert 42.5 mL to 0.0425 L, then multiply by the molarity.

bank.question: A diluted bleach solution has [OH<sup>−</sup>] = 1.9 × 10<sup>−4</sup> M at 25 °C. What is [H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>]?
bank.new_reason: This divides [OH<sup>−</sup>] by K<sub>w</sub>. Put K<sub>w</sub> on top: [H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>] = 1.0 × 10<sup>−14</sup> ÷ [OH<sup>−</sup>].

bank.question: An over-the-counter fluoride mouth rinse is 0.050% (m/v) sodium fluoride, NaF. How many grams of NaF are in a 10.0 mL dose?
bank.new_reason: This divides by 100 twice. 0.050% (m/v) means 0.050 g per 100 mL, so multiply 10.0 mL by 0.050 g / 100 mL once.

bank.question: How many potassium ions are in 1.49 g of potassium chloride, KCl (74.55 g/mol)?
bank.new_reason: This counts both K<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>. Each KCl gives one K<sup>+</sup>, so use a 1 : 1 ratio and do not double the count.

bank.question: Heating potassium chlorate releases oxygen: 2 KClO<sub>3</sub>(s) → 2 KCl(s) + 3 O<sub>2</sub>(g). What volume of O<sub>2</sub> at 1.02 atm and 22.5 °C forms from 4.25 g of KClO<sub>3</sub> (122.55 g/mol)?
bank.new_reason: This uses the Celsius temperature. Gas laws need kelvins: add 273.15 to 22.5 °C before using PV = nRT.

bank.question: A 12.5 L tank holds 0.645 mol of oxygen at 24.5 °C. What is the pressure in the tank?
bank.new_reason: This uses the Celsius temperature. Gas laws need kelvins: add 273.15 to 24.5 °C before using PV = nRT.

bank.question: Thorium-232, found in many rocks, is an alpha emitter. Which equation is balanced?
bank.new_reason: Bottom: 89 + 2 = 91, not 90. Alpha emission lowers Z by 2, so the product's atomic number must be 90 − 2.

bank.question: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes on a wound: 2 H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>(aq) → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l) + O<sub>2</sub>(g). What mass of H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> (34.014 g/mol) must decompose to give 1.45 L of O<sub>2</sub> at 0.978 atm and 24.5 °C?
bank.new_reason: This skips the mole ratio. Multiply moles of O<sub>2</sub> by 2 mol H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> / 1 mol O<sub>2</sub> before converting to grams.

bank.question: Valley dried-fruit packers treat apricots with sulfur dioxide gas to keep their color. What is the formula of sulfur dioxide?
bank.new_reason: Di- means two oxygen atoms. Turn each prefix into a subscript: no prefix on sulfur means 1 S, and dioxide means O<sub>2</sub>.

bank.question: Zinc reacts with acid, Zn(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → ZnCl<sub>2</sub>(aq) + H<sub>2</sub>(g), and 62.5 mL of H<sub>2</sub> is collected over water at 30.0 °C. The barometer reads 765 mmHg, and water's vapor pressure at 30.0 °C is 31.8 mmHg. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub> were collected?
bank.new_reason: This uses mL as liters. Convert 62.5 mL to 0.0625 L before using PV = nRT.

bank.question: A solution is made by dissolving 6.40 g of potassium iodide, KI, in 145.0 g of water. What is the mass percent of KI?
bank.new_reason: This is the percent of water. Put the mass of KI on top and the mass of the whole solution (KI + water) on the bottom.

bank.question: A 6.50 L steel tank holds 0.312 mol of nitrogen at 1.27 atm. What is the temperature in kelvins?
bank.new_reason: This is nR/(PV), the reciprocal. Solve PV = nRT for T: T = PV / (nR).

bank.question: What is [H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>] in 0.0082 M KOH at 25 °C?
bank.new_reason: This multiplies by K<sub>w</sub>. KOH gives [OH<sup>−</sup>] = 0.0082 M, so [H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>] = 1.0 × 10<sup>−14</sup> ÷ 0.0082.

bank.question: Radiologic technologists wear aprons made with lead to shield their bodies. What is the symbol for lead?
bank.worked: Lead is Pb, from the Latin plumbum. Pd is palladium and P is phosphorus.
bank.new_reason: P is phosphorus, a nonmetal. Lead's symbol comes from its Latin name, plumbum, so look for the symbol that starts with Pb.

bank.question: In a gas-production lab, magnesium ribbon reacts with acid: Mg(s) + 2 HCl(aq) → MgCl<sub>2</sub>(aq) + H<sub>2</sub>(g). What volume of H<sub>2</sub>, in mL at STP, forms from 0.0425 g of Mg? (Mg 24.31 g/mol)
bank.worked: 0.0425 g Mg × (1 mol / 24.31 g) × (1 mol H2 / 1 mol Mg) × (22.4 L / 1 mol) = 0.03916 L = 39.2 mL H2.
bank.new_reason: This stops at moles of H<sub>2</sub>. Multiply by 22.4 L/mol, then convert liters to mL.

bank.question: The thermite reaction welds railroad rails: 2 Al(s) + Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>(s) → Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>(s) + 2 Fe(s). What is the oxidizing agent?
bank.worked: Al: 0 → +3 (oxidized; reducing agent). Fe: +3 → 0 (reduced). Oxidizing agent: Fe2O3.
bank.new_reason: Fe is a product, and the oxidizing agent is a reactant. Find the reactant whose atoms are reduced (Fe +3 → 0).

bank.question: What mass of potassium iodide, KI (166.00 g/mol), contains 0.100 g of iodine? (I 126.90)
bank.worked: 0.100 g I × (1 mol I / 126.90 g) × (1 mol KI / 1 mol I) × (166.00 g / 1 mol KI) = 0.131 g KI. (Potassium iodide tablets for radiation emergencies are about 130 mg for about 100 mg of iodide; context only.)
bank.new_reason: This stops at moles of iodine. Use the 1 mol KI : 1 mol I ratio, then multiply by 166.00 g/mol to get grams of KI.
